To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
delayed delivery is associated to a higher survival rate of the remaining multiple(s), and that this is more evident when the first twin is born before 24 weeks of pregnancy.
delayed deliveries in twin and triplet pregnancies should be considered as a viable option in case of a preterm birth of the first twin.

delayed delivery of the second twin is a safe procedure that should be performed in all cases of multifetal pregnancy with asynchronous births, provided that a strict monitoring of maternal and fetal well-being is guaranteed.

the management of asynchronous delivery in multiple pregnancies.
the development of an effective and efficient algorithm for managing the asynchronous deliveries of multiple pregnancies, with a focus on the delivery of the second twin.
the management of multiple pregnancy, and in particular with the management of the delayed birth of the second twin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the delay of the second twin's birth is recommended when the first is born at a gestational age of 24 weeks or later, but the decision must be taken on an individual basis, considering all possible risks and benefits for the mother and the remaining fetuses.
, when possible, it is better to delay delivery of the remaining multiples, even if this is associated with a higher risk of chorioamnioitis, because this will improve the outcome of pre-term birth.

, if the first twin is born before 24 weeks of GA, the remaining twin or higher-order multiples should be delivered as soon as possible; whereas if the first twin was delivered after 24 weeks, the second one should be delivered within 2-3 weeks, or at least within 4-5 weeks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
delayed delivery of remaining multiple gestation after the birth of the first twin is an effective strategy to improve the outcome of the remaining fetuses.
, in multiple pregnancies, the delivery of the remaining fetuses should be delayed as long as possible, in order to improve survival rates.
delayed delivery of higher-order multiples is associated with higher survival rates of the second twin and other higher-order multiples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in case of delayed delivery in multifetal pregnancy, the survival rate increases with the delay of the second birth, but the shorter is the interval between births.
, in case of delayed delivery of multiple pregnancies, there is an advantage to delay delivery of the remaining multiples, as long as this improves the outcome of pre-term birth.
, in the case of delayed delivery of multiple pregnancies, the survival rate is higher if the delivery of the remaining multiple(s) is postponed, even in the presence of chorioamnititis.
